Definition: Adna, the name of two Israelites
BiblicalUsage: Adna is the name of two Israelites: one of the sons of Pahath-moab who had taken a foreign wife in Ezra's day and put her away, and a priest, head of the house of Harim, in the days of Joiakim the high priest. The two men share a name and nothing else — one in a list of repentance, one in a list of priests.
TheologicalSignificance: A shared name across two lists carries no teaching, and I won't invent one. Taken together, the two Adnas show the two sides of the return: putting away what God forbade, and keeping the priesthood in order for worship to go on.
RelatedPeople: Adna, Son of Pahath-moab; Adna, of Harim's Course
